review_notes: Read the whole target file and the IsCentrePre API (Sec12Defs, Sec7Basic). Looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning. The only repetition that recurs, both inside this file and in many others, is converting between IsCentrePre membership and the flipped commutator ⁅g, x⁆ ∈ Q. Each instance is short, so the case is modest. The proofs in this file are otherwise distinct: centModQ closure, the CN-centre argument, and the hZL argument are not duplicated elsewhere in the file. I did not search every file for a near-duplicate of the larger hZL argument. I could not compile the proposed lemma.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out at least four times in this file (lines 108-113, 128-130, 141-142, 143-145), and again at lines 97-99. Each time it goes between `x ∈ Z0` for `IsCentrePre Z0 R Q` and the flipped-commutator condition `∀ g ∈ R, ⁅g, x⁆ ∈ Q`. It rewrites with `← commutatorElement_inv` and applies `Q.inv_mem`. Because `IsCentrePre` is defined with `⁅x, r⁆`, every caller repeats this symmetry step by hand. The same three-line pattern appears in other files: Sec7CommN.lean line 46, HeringSec91CentreL.lean line 118, Sec7Index.lean, Sec78ZtCore.lean and Sec84Basic.lean. The repetition is a maintenance cost, and it clutters the actual mathematical content of each proof.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas next to `IsCentrePre.comm_mem` in Sec7Basic.lean:
`theorem IsCentrePre.comm_mem' {Z0 R Q : Subgroup G} [Q.Normal-free, no hypothesis needed] (h : IsCentrePre Z0 R Q) {x r : G} (hx : x ∈ Z0) (hr : r ∈ R) : ⁅r, x⁆ ∈ Q`, proved by `rw [← commutatorElement_inv]; exact Q.inv_mem (h.comm_mem hx hr)`.
`theorem IsCentrePre.mem_of_comm' {Z0 R Q : Subgroup G} (h : IsCentrePre Z0 R Q) {x : G} (hxR : x ∈ R) (hc : ∀ r ∈ R, ⁅r, x⁆ ∈ Q) : x ∈ Z0`, proved by `(h x).mpr ⟨hxR, fun r hr => by rw [← commutatorElement_inv]; exact Q.inv_mem (hc r hr)⟩`.
Then rewrite the uses here:
- line 97-99: `have h2 : ⁅l, s⁆ ∈ Q := hZ0.comm_mem' hs0 (hLR hl)`.
- line 108-113: `have hbZ0 : b ∈ Z0 := hZ0.mem_of_comm' (hL'R hb.1) (fun g hg => by rw [hr.gen] at hg; exact (hle hg).2)`.
- line 128-130: `exact hZ0.mem_of_comm' (hLR hx.1) (fun g hg => hcomm g hg x hx)`.
- lines 139-145: use `fun hx => ⟨hZL hx, fun g hg => hZ0.comm_mem' hx hg⟩` and `fun ⟨hxL, hxg⟩ => hZ0.mem_of_comm' (le_Rt (M := M) (LB M Q B) ht hxL) hxg`.
The other files listed above can use the same lemmas.
findings.benefit: The commutator-inversion step is proved once instead of being re-derived in each caller. The proofs here shrink by about a dozen lines, and each proof states directly that it uses centrality modulo Q. The recurring pattern across the Stroth80 files gets one named API entry, which reduces mistakes and makes later changes to the `IsCentrePre` convention local.
